record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Given a field k of positive characteristic, classify all regular injections of the affine line A^1_k into the affine plane A^2_k.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM. Given a ﬁeld k of positive characteristic, classify all possible regular injections of the aﬃne line A1 k into the aﬃne plane A2 k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic, and let $\mathbb{A}^n_k = \operatorname{Spec} k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ denote affine $n$-space over $k$. A regular injection (closed embedding) of the affine line into the affine plane is a morphism $\varphi : \mathbb{A}^1_k \to \mathbb{A}^2_k$ of $k$-schemes given by $t \mapsto (f(t), g(t))$ with $f,g \in k[t]$, such that $\varphi$ induces an isomorphism of $\mathbb{A}^1_k$ onto its scheme-theoretic image (equivalently, the induced ring homomorphism $k[x,y] \to k[t]$, $x \mapsto f$, $y \mapsto g$, is surjective). Two such embeddings $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ are called equivalent if there exists a $k$-algebra automorphism $\Phi$ of $k[x,y]$ such that $\varphi_2 = \Phi \circ \varphi_1$. 

In characteristic zero, the Abhyankar–Moh–Suzuki theorem asserts that every such embedding is equivalent to the standard embedding $t \mapsto (t,0)$. In positive characteristic this fails: there exist embeddings (for instance certain ones involving Frobenius-type polynomials) that are inequivalent to the standard one. 

Problem: Give a complete classification, up to the above equivalence by polynomial automorphisms of $\mathbb{A}^2_k$, of all regular injections $\mathbb{A}^1_k \hookrightarrow \mathbb{A}^2_k$ when $k$ is a field of positive characteristic.
artifact.category_tag: embeddings of affine line in affine plane
artifact.status_search_result: The classical Abhyankar–Moh–Suzuki theorem resolves the analogous classification in characteristic zero, but in positive characteristic non-equivalent ("exotic") embeddings are known to exist, and no complete classification has been established. The literature continues to study examples and partial results (e.g., embeddings into complements of conics), indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Abhyankar–Moh theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The theorem applies to lines and planes over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero
status_evidence.claim: The Abhyankar–Moh classification result is restricted to characteristic zero, leaving the positive characteristic case unsettled.

status_evidence.title: AFFINE LINES IN THE COMPLEMENT OF A SMOOTH PLANE CONIC
status_evidence.snippet: Over fields of positive characteristic there exist exotic closed embeddings of the affine line
status_evidence.claim: Exotic closed embeddings of A^1 exist in positive characteristic, showing classification is strictly harder than in char 0 and is still being investigated.
